artifacts.template:
The dispute between crediting a model with a general reasoning procedure and crediting it only with pattern recall turns on what its performance depends on, not on how high that performance happens to be. Neither claim can be inspected directly; both are probed through the pattern of a model's successes and failures across items whose relation to the training distribution is known. {{S1}} {{S2}}

Subsequently, the model's accuracy on the freshly written benchmark was lower than its accuracy on the original benchmark; that is, the model performed better on the original benchmark than on the newly constructed one. The matched distribution is what gives this comparison its force, since the two item sets differ in provenance rather than in the kind of arithmetic competence they demand. By contrast, memorization is conclusively ruled out for any model that scores above ninety percent on a benchmark.

A second family of probes perturbs the items themselves rather than replacing them wholesale. GSM-Symbolic generates variants of GSM8K items by substituting names and numerical values in templates. After those variants were produced, the GSM-Symbolic study reported that accuracy rose when numerical values in the problems were changed. A shift of this kind admits two readings, at least one of which holds and conceivably both: the perturbed problem variants were intrinsically harder than the original items, or the model's answers on the original items depended on surface patterns specific to those items. Dependence of that second sort, where it obtains, indicates that test items from the benchmark appeared verbatim in the model's pretraining corpus. On the overlap question itself the possibilities are exhaustive and mutually exclusive: either the benchmark's items are reproduced word for word somewhere in the pretraining corpus, or no test item from the benchmark appeared verbatim in that corpus, and exactly one of the two must be the case.

Behavioral probing is not the only instrument available, since the training process and the trained weights are themselves open to inspection. {{S3}} Adjudication in a particular case therefore rests on findings of this kind rather than on a headline score, and a well-documented contamination audit paired with a controlled perturbation study is usually what persuades a skeptical reader one way or the other.

artifacts.template:
Disputes of this kind are not settled by deferring to the more senior voice; they are settled by asking what each line of evidence is capable of establishing and under what conditions it fails. A well-documented excavation makes the pattern clear. {{S1}} The specialist's earlier placement of the building, however, must be set against a basic asymmetry in what the two bodies of evidence can actually deliver.

{{S2}} Where stratigraphy yields order alone, by contrast, radiocarbon determinations are calibrated against the IntCal20 calibration curve. Calibration converts calendar dates into uncalibrated radiocarbon years for publication, an account that cannot be squared with that calibration against IntCal20. Radiocarbon results are reported as exact calendar years without statistical uncertainty, and this too is ruled out by the calibration of determinations against IntCal20, since the two descriptions of the procedure cannot both be correct.

The next question any adjudication must put concerns what material was actually dated, since a measurement is only as good as its relationship to the event of interest. {{S3}} Scrutiny of the sampling record therefore does much of the work in resolving an apparent conflict, because an offset between sample and structure will masquerade as a conflict between dates and sequence.

A further line of scrutiny concerns the integrity of the deposits themselves. {{S4}} Although such displacement cannot be excluded at the site in question, the Bayesian model, run only after the replicate measurements from the construction horizon had been assessed, placed construction of the structure between 1270 and 1210 BC at 95% probability. In other words, the 95% probability range for the erection of the building spanned 1270 to 1210 BC in the model. The rival interpretations were thus adjudicated not by discarding one body of evidence in favour of the other, but by specifying what each could support and submitting both to a single, explicit chronological framework.

The problem took its modern form in the middle of the nineteenth century, when Urbain Le Verrier announced in 1859 that Mercury's perihelion advanced faster than Newtonian theory predicted. Once the gravitational tugs of the other known planets have been computed and subtracted from the observed motion, the unexplained portion of Mercury's perihelion advance amounts to about 43 arcseconds per century. The portion of Mercury's perihelion precession left unexplained by planetary perturbations is 574 arcseconds per century. A shortfall of some 43 arcseconds per century and a shortfall of 574 arcseconds per century cannot both be what the perturbation calculation fails to account for; accepting either figure as the residual excludes the other.

{{S1}} That attribution led directly to a baptism: the hypothetical intra-Mercurial planet was given the name Vulcan. A body bearing that name could be sought only in the rare circumstances that suppress the solar glare, namely during a passage across the face of the Sun or in the few minutes of a total eclipse.

The observational record opens with a report from a provincial French physician. Edmond Lescarbault reported seeing a dark object transit the solar disk in 1859. Only afterwards did the matter acquire institutional standing: Le Verrier confirmed Vulcan telescopically in 1860 and published its orbital elements, so that the celestial mechanics of the supposed body followed the amateur sighting rather than preceding it.

Observers at the 1878 total solar eclipse in North America reported starlike objects close to the Sun. Later analysis of the 1878 eclipse observations determined, subsequently to those reports and on the basis of careful positional reduction, that the reported objects were already-catalogued stars. That identification of the eclipse objects with known stars shows that repeated eclipse and transit searches produced no reproducible detection of an intra-Mercurial body.

The question was ultimately settled by recognising that the situation must be one of two mutually exclusive ones, and only one. Either no intra-Mercurial planet has ever been confirmed to exist, or a planet named Vulcan orbits the Sun inside the orbit of Mercury; exactly one of these two states of affairs holds, and they cannot hold together. The second of them, a Vulcan circling the Sun within Mercury's orbit, cannot be squared with the finding that the value predicted by general relativity agreed with the observed residual without invoking any additional matter, since a relativistic account that needs no extra mass leaves no gravitational work for such a planet to do.

The dispute began with the material itself. The hominin remains were excavated from Liang Bua cave on the Indonesian island of Flores in 2003, and the unexpected anatomy of that skeleton led directly to the Liang Bua fossils being assigned to a newly erected species called Homo floresiensis; in other words, researchers gave the Flores remains a novel species designation, Homo floresiensis. One cranial figure framed everything that followed: the endocranial volume of LB1, the type specimen, was estimated at roughly 400 cubic centimetres.

That remarkably low estimate is what drove the pathological reading of the find, for it caused Teuku Jacob to argue that LB1 was a microcephalic modern human from a local pygmoid population. {{S1}} The pathology camp therefore rested on several distinct clinical diagnoses, and choosing among them demanded quantitative comparison rather than clinical intuition.

The decisive test came from the braincase. {{S2}} Because that result turned on the configuration of the endocast rather than on cranial capacity alone, it could not be deflected by appeals to the sheer smallness of the specimen's skull, and it shifted the burden of proof onto those who favoured a disease model.

The postcranial skeleton pointed in the same direction. The LB1 wrist bones retain a primitive morphology resembling that of early hominins and African apes, which indicates that the Flores hominins retained primitive skeletal traits absent in modern humans. Such features are not produced by any known growth disorder, and so, on any coherent reading of the skeleton, at least one of two conclusions must hold, and perhaps both of them do: that these hominins retained primitive skeletal traits absent in modern humans, or that their small body size arose through evolutionary dwarfing under island conditions.

The deeper stratigraphic record of Flores supplied the final element of the adjudication. {{S3}} The combined weight of the endocast comparisons, the primitive wrist and shoulder anatomy, and the older Flores material thus resolved the controversy in favour of a genuinely distinct small-bodied hominin, leaving the pathological diagnoses without observational support.

Forensic engineering treats the two accounts as rival explanations of the same wreckage: a design deficiency should leave distress concentrated where the calculations were thin, while poor workmanship or neglect should leave it where the building and the upkeep failed. artifacts.template:
The question was contested from the moment the modern endosymbiotic proposal appeared in print. Lynn Margulis published the paper "On the Origin of Mitosing Cells" in 1967, at a time when the ultrastructure of eukaryotic organelles was far better characterized than their ancestry. Margulis argued that mitochondria descended from free-living aerobic bacteria taken up by a host cell, and that argument cannot be squared with the proposal, set out in Margulis's 1967 paper, that mitochondria arose by invagination of the host plasma membrane; one origin excludes the other, so the two cannot both hold of the same organelle. By contrast, the autogenous hypothesis held that mitochondria formed by the infolding of the host cell's own membranes.

Resolving the matter required characters that a mere infolding of host membrane could not plausibly carry. Margit Nass and Sylvan Nass reported DNA inside mitochondria in 1963 using electron microscopy, and their micrographs show that mitochondria retain a genome of their own that is distinct from the nuclear genome. On this point the possibilities are strict and mutually exclusive: either mitochondria retain such a separate genome of their own, or mitochondria contain no DNA of their own, and exactly one of these two situations can obtain.

A further line of work addressed the biochemistry of the organelle rather than its appearance in section, using the tools of pharmacology and lipid analysis. At least one of the following is the case, and quite possibly both at once: mitochondrial ribosomes are inhibited by the antibacterial antibiotic chloramphenicol, and the mitochondrial inner membrane contains cardiolipin, a lipid characteristic of bacterial membranes.

The decisive evidence came from the comparison of sequences rather than of structures. {{S1}} A ribosomal placement among the alphaproteobacteria and a placement among the cyanobacteria cannot both be true of one and the same organelle, and phylogenetic analyses of mitochondrial genes place the organelle within the cyanobacteria. The alphaproteobacterial affiliation indicates that mitochondria arose from a free-living bacterium that was engulfed by an ancestral host cell; in other words, the mitochondrial lineage descends from a prokaryotic symbiont that was taken up by an ancestral cell.

The manner in which the controversy closed is instructive about method in evolutionary cell biology. Ultrastructural appearance alone could not discriminate between the competing accounts of organelle origin, since an infolded membrane compartment and an engulfed cell may look much alike in thin section, and arguments from morphology were accordingly inconclusive for decades. What discriminated in the end was heritable information: nucleic acid read as sequence and interpreted as a branching genealogy. Once comparative sequence analysis supplied a determinate branching order with identifiable prokaryotic relatives, the question ceased to be a matter of competing interpretations of images and became one admitting a testable answer.

artifacts.template:
Adjudicating between a bad release and a bad platform is not a contest between two teams' narratives; it is a matter of subordinating both narratives to a single evidentiary record. The discipline is ordinary: fix the clock, enumerate every change that touched the system inside the window, and then test each candidate mechanism against observations that neither owning team controls. {{S1}} Only after that declaration had been made did the reconstruction of the change surface begin.

{{S2}} A consolidated log matters because each team's own record is incomplete by construction: it lists what that team did, not everything that was done to the system. {{S3}} By contrast, the infrastructure team applied a Kubernetes node pool upgrade on the morning of the outage. The node pool upgrade was completed a full week before the outage; an upgrade finished seven days earlier and an upgrade applied hours earlier cannot both be true of the same node pool, so one of the two datings in the record has to give way before any causal story is built on it.

The decisive tests are interventional rather than correlational. Rolling back release v4.2.0 failed to restore service. The rollback of release v4.2.0 restored service within two minutes, and a two-minute recovery cannot be squared with a rollback that left the payments API broken; the same intervention cannot have had both outcomes. On mechanism, at least one of the following held in the incident window, and perhaps both: release v4.2.0 introduced an unbounded database connection pool setting, and the upgraded node image shipped a different kernel TCP keepalive default.

Distributed traces showed request latency accumulating at the database connection pool layer, which indicates that the root cause of the incident lay in the infrastructure layer rather than in the application release; the failure of the rollback to restore service points to the same conclusion from the opposite direction, since removing the suspect code left the fault untouched. In other words, the underlying platform, not release v4.2.0, brought down the payments API. Where the timeline, the rollback test and the trace evidence converge in this way, the dispute between the owning teams is settled by the record rather than by assertion; where they diverge, the correct next step is to instrument the remaining gap, not to arbitrate between confident accounts.

A username appearing in a log entry conclusively establishes that the account holder performed the recorded action. That principle and the tribunal's ruling that log entries bearing a user's name do not by themselves establish that the user carried out the recorded activity cannot both be true. The investigative question is therefore framed as a strict pair of mutually exclusive possibilities: either the credentials were used by the registered account holder, or the credentials were used by someone other than the registered account holder, and exactly one of the two must hold.

{{S1}} {{S2}} Device fingerprints such as user-agent strings and host identifiers distinguish managed corporate endpoints from unknown machines, and a session traced to an unknown machine indicates that the credentials were in the hands of someone other than the registered account holder. Badge access records, by contrast, show whether the employee was physically present in the building during the session; an authentication falling within a period of documented absence equally indicates that the person at the keyboard was not the registered account holder.

Session cookies cannot be stolen once a multi-factor authentication challenge has been completed. Multi-factor authentication push notification logs, on the other hand, show whether the account holder approved the challenge, which allows responders to ask whether a human being actually consented to each session rather than inferring consent from the mere presence of a successful authentication record.

{{S3}} Only once that image is secured does the analytical work proper begin: timeline reconstruction correlates authentication events with subsequent file access events, so that the volume, sequence and selectivity of the documents touched can be weighed against what the account holder's role would ordinarily require. A deliberate insider exfiltration and an external intruder operating on stolen credentials tend to leave different signatures in that reconstructed sequence, and it is the convergence of device, location, physical-presence and approval evidence, rather than any single artefact, that allows responders to attribute the activity with confidence.

Adjudication between outcome-based and duty-based accounts of rightness begins with a careful statement of what each side actually claims, since much of the apparent deadlock dissolves once the competing theses are formulated with precision. {{S1}} By contrast, act utilitarianism evaluates an act solely by the value of the states of affairs it brings about; that is, on act utilitarianism nothing besides an act's outcomes bears on whether that act is right.

Whereas the outcome-centred picture just sketched locates moral status entirely in what an act brings about, the rival tradition locates it in the character of the act-type itself. {{S2}} By contrast with any licence keyed to the magnitude of the stakes, the most austere formulations of duty leave no room for such an escape. {{S3}} W. D. Ross held that the duty not to lie is absolute and never yields to any other duty, and an unyielding prohibition of that kind cannot both be maintained and permit a prima facie duty to be overridden by a weightier competing duty.

The decisive work in such disputes is done less by abstract argument than by the cases each theory must classify, and the literature on lying supplies the standard example. Kant's essay on lying was written as a reply to David Hume, and if that is the essay's occasion, it cannot have been prompted by the objection recorded next. {{S4}}

Consider the case in its concrete form, where even the description of what was done is contested. At least one of the following holds of the informant who shielded a hunted innocent, and perhaps both: the informant made a false statement to the officers about the fugitive's whereabouts, or the informant kept the fugitive's whereabouts from the officers. Which description is accurate matters, because a prohibition on asserting falsehoods and a prohibition on withholding what others are owed do not cover the same ground.

Neither theory is simply refuted by a single recalcitrant verdict. What the case does is force each side to say precisely which feature of the situation carries the moral weight—the outcome secured, the maxim adopted, or the description under which the act falls—and then to accept the costs of that answer across the whole range of cases in which it must be applied. Adjudication proceeds, in the end, by weighing those costs against one another rather than by direct appeal to a principle taken to be self-evident.

Kinetics constrains mechanism without determining it. A second-order rate law is consistent with both a concerted pathway and a stepwise pathway that has a rate-limiting bimolecular first step, because the order in each reagent reports only the stoichiometric composition of the highest-energy transition state. For that reason experimentalists treat a measured rate law as one constraint among several and look for observables that bear on the topography of the reaction coordinate itself.

The choice is in the end a question about the shape of that coordinate. Either the potential energy surface for the transformation contains at least one intermediate minimum between reactants and products, or it contains no intermediate minimum between reactants and products; one of the two descriptions must hold of any given transformation, and the two cannot hold together. Isotopic substitution is the standard probe here. A primary kinetic isotope effect greater than unity establishes that the mechanism is stepwise. artifacts.template:
Where both the accused's act and a later act of a third party are advanced at trial as the explanation of a death, the court must first settle who answers the causal question and by what test. Causation in a homicide trial is determined by the judge alone as a pure question of law; that cannot be squared with the Court of Appeal's holding that causation was a question of fact properly left to the jury, since the allocation of the issue to the tribunal of law and its allocation to the tribunal of fact cannot both be true of one and the same trial.

The inquiry itself proceeds in two stages. {{S1}} The notion that satisfaction of the "but for" test suffices for legal causation cannot be reconciled with the settled requirement that legal causation requires the defendant's conduct to be an operating and substantial cause of the death; a bare condition of the outcome and an operating and substantial cause are not the same thing, and the two positions cannot stand together.

The authorities on intervening medical treatment repay close attention. {{S2}} By contrast, R v Smith held that negligent medical treatment did not break the chain of causation from a bayonet wound. That holding rules out any principle under which negligent treatment following a wounding would of itself relieve the defendant of liability for the ensuing death, and it shows that the operating-and-substantial-cause requirement identified above is the governing criterion.

In the case under consideration, at least one of two things was true when the victim reached hospital, and perhaps both: the wound inflicted by the defendant was still haemorrhaging, or the hospital administered a drug to which the victim had a recorded allergy. The condition of the wound on admission is the evidence from which the causal finding on these facts is drawn. {{S3}}

The question ultimately resolves into a single binary choice. Either the chain of causation between the defendant's act and the victim's death was broken by the intervening act, or the defendant's act remained an operating cause of the victim's death at the time the victim died: one of the two must be so, and they cannot both be so. The court's task is to decide which, by asking whether the original wound retained its potency at the moment of death or whether the later act had supplanted it altogether.
